questions.question: Which histological subtype of lung cancer is the most common overall and typically presents as a peripheral mass?
questions.detail: Adenocarcinoma has overtaken squamous cell as the most common subtype and usually originates in the lung periphery.

questions.question: A 65-year-old heavy smoker presents with a large, centrally located mass that shows central cavitation. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.detail: Squamous cell carcinoma is strongly associated with smoking, occurs centrally, and is the subtype most likely to cavitate.

questions.question: Which type of lung cancer is considered a "surgical" disease at early stages but frequently presents with paraneoplastic syndromes like Hypercalcemia (PTHrP)?
questions.detail: Squamous cell is associated with PTHrP-induced hypercalcemia, whereas small cell is more associated with ACTH (Cushing) and ADH (SIADH).

questions.question: According to the current TNM staging, a tumor measuring 2.5 cm in its greatest dimension with no other suspicious features is classified as:
questions.detail: T1 staging is strictly based on size: T1a is ≤1 cm, T1b is >1 to 2 cm, and T1c is >2 to 3 cm.

questions.question: A tumor that invades the chest wall or parietal pleura is automatically staged as at least:
questions.detail: T3 classification includes invasion of the chest wall, pericardium, or phrenic nerve, or satellite nodules in the same lobe.

questions.question: Nodal staging for lung cancer uses specific anatomical levels. Involvement of the ipsilateral hilar nodes (levels 10–14) is classified as:
questions.detail: N1 nodal involvement is defined by the presence of disease in ipsilateral hilar and intrapulmonary nodes.

questions.question: What anatomical landmark defines the boundary between the right and left for level 2 and 4 (paratracheal) lymph nodes?
choices: The right lateral border of the trachea
The left lateral border of the trachea
questions.detail: The left lateral border of the trachea serves as the anatomical boundary due to the specific flow of lymphatic drainage.

questions.question: Involvement of the subcarinal lymph nodes (Level 7) in a patient with a right-sided lung cancer is classified as:
questions.detail: Level 7 (subcarinal) nodes are considered ipsilateral mediastinal nodes (N2) for tumors located on either side of the chest.

questions.question: Metastasis to a contralateral hilar or contralateral mediastinal lymph node is classified as:
questions.detail: N3 is defined by involvement of any contralateral node or any supraclavicular node, whether ipsilateral or contralateral.

questions.question: A patient with a 4 cm tumor in the right upper lobe also has a separate 1 cm nodule in the right lower lobe. What is the T-stage?
questions.detail: A satellite nodule in the same lobe is staged as T3, but a separate nodule in a different ipsilateral lobe is staged as T4.

questions.question: Which metastatic stage (M-stage) describes a nodule in the contralateral lung?
questions.detail: M1a staging includes pleural or pericardial nodules or effusions, as well as nodules found in the contralateral lung.

questions.question: What is the most common benign calcification pattern in a solitary pulmonary nodule (SPN), often described as "popcorn" calcification?
questions.detail: Popcorn calcification is considered pathognomonic for a hamartoma. Central, diffuse, and laminated are other typically benign patterns.

questions.question: An SPN showing an "eccentric" or stippled calcification pattern is concerning for:
questions.detail: Eccentric or stippled calcification patterns are considered suspicious for malignancy and may represent a tumor engulfing a benign calcified nodule.

questions.question: A Superior Sulcus (Pancoast) tumor is classically associated with which clinical syndrome?
questions.detail: Pancoast tumors can invade the sympathetic chain, resulting in Horner syndrome (ptosis, miosis, and anhidrosis).

questions.question: In staging Small Cell Lung Cancer (SCLC), "limited stage" disease is defined as:
choices: Safe to treat within a single radiation portal
Confined to the lung parenchyma only
questions.detail: Limited stage disease is confined to one hemithorax and its regional nodes, meaning it can be encompassed in a single radiation field.

questions.question: Which sign on CT involves a pulmonary artery branch leading directly into a peripheral nodule?
questions.detail: The feeding vessel sign is characteristic of hematogenous processes such as septic emboli and hematogenous metastases.

questions.question: Which paraneoplastic syndrome is most strongly associated with Small Cell Lung Cancer?
questions.detail: As a neuroendocrine tumor, small cell carcinoma frequently produces ADH (causing SIADH) or ACTH.

questions.question: What is the current recommended screening method for lung cancer in high-risk patients?
questions.detail: Annual low-dose non-contrast CT has been proven to reduce mortality in high-risk smokers.
